title: ‘Girls’ to Return for a Limited Run
partialText: HBO announced that the show created by Lena Dunham will begin production on five new episodes next year, 10 years after the finale.

title: The New Yorker Cartoonist P.C. Vey Has Died
partialText: His work for The New Yorker savaged the absurdities of everyday life. He has died at 70.

title: Judy Markey, Frank and Funny Voice on Chicago Radio, Dies at 82
partialText: She and Kathy O’Malley — known as “the Girlfriends” — were the rare female hosts in a major market. Their freewheeling segments included “Sex Thursday.”

title: War Collides With Saudi Ambition at a Gathering of Oil Powers
partialText: The tone of the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh this week was defiant even as delegates were forced to redirect travel or address the audience from afar.

title: Rising Interest Rates Bite Some Wall St. Banks
partialText: JPMorgan released surprisingly spotty earnings results for the third quarter, while Goldman Sachs and Citi posted better-than-expected results, reflecting a choppy trading environment.

title: Vance, Altman, Musk, Mamdani, Bieber and More at the DealBook Summit
partialText: The conference on Nov. 18 will bring together the biggest names in business, politics, culture and more

title: Chip Stocks Tumble on A.I. Spending Fears and Rising Chinese Competition
partialText: South Korean stocks tumbled in particular, as reports of a breakthrough by a Chinese chip rival heightened concerns about competition.

title: Hillary Clinton Steps to the Podcast Mic as Midterms Approach
partialText: With “High Stakes,” Mrs. Clinton is teaming up with “Pivot” co-host Kara Swisher to break down the consequential battle for the House and the Senate.

title: How Climate Change Is Causing ‘the Gentrification of Seafood’
partialText: As environmental forces make fishing and harvesting more costly, the price of once-everyday fish has ballooned.

title: The Forces Driving Up Bond Yields Take a Troubling Turn
partialText: Some analysts say investors are demanding a higher “term premium” to buy government debt, reflecting growing worries about debt levels and deficits.

title: How Two Crypto Billionaires Are Making British Politics More American
partialText: A pair of low-profile entrepreneurs gave $100 million to Nigel Farage’s Reform U.K. Party. The system may never be the same.

title: States Now Have to Decide How to Spend Meta’s Settlement Billions
partialText: Previous agreements with the tobacco and opioid industries show the difficulty of putting the money in the right hands.

title: I.M.F. Warns Mideast War Will Widen Gap Between Rich and Poor Countries
partialText: Persistent conflicts, high energy costs and technological upheavals will slow global growth and raise prices, the organization forecast.

title: Police Identify 42-Year Old Man Killed at Six Flags Over Georgia
partialText: The police identified the 42-year-old man who died at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday. The company said it was temporarily closing multiple rides in the U.S. and Canada as a precaution.

title: How American Retirees at Different Incomes Rely on Social Security
partialText: Social Security funds are on track to run short by 2032, which would mean a reduction in benefits. Here’s how four hypothetical households rely on the program in retirement.

title: Europeans Have a Love-Hate Relationship With Chinese Cars
partialText: Consumers across the continent increasingly want to buy low-cost Chinese vehicles. Policymakers are seeking to slow them down.

title: Strikes Put Saudi Arabia’s Economy Under Pressure
partialText: Deadly attacks on the main Saudi airport add to the challenges facing the country, as it seeks to maintain energy production and keep major events on track.

title: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford Awarded Nobel for Economics
partialText: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford were awarded the prize for insights that helped policymakers become “better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy,” the committee said.

title: World’s Energy Order Tested Again as Iran War’s Reach Extends Further
partialText: “We are entering an age of prolonged insecurity,” one former U.S. energy official said of what have become chronic threats on the Middle East’s energy core.

title: America’s Favorite Fruit Is Being Bruised by the Iran War
partialText: The journey of one banana from farm to store shows how the war’s economic effects have cascaded into some surprising industries.

title: A Contagious Aversion to Overhead Lights
partialText: Plus: How far to go for a colleague, and now your chance to give someone advice.

title: Three Mark Zuckerbergs, Three Surprisingly Different Men
partialText: Jeremy Strong in “The Social Reckoning,” Jesse Eisenberg in “The Social Network” and the real Meta executive are all playing parts. But only one has changed his approach.

title: San Francisco Is Still Pushing to Turn Offices Into Homes
partialText: The city has not completed a single office-to-housing conversion, despite hopes to meet housing demand and inject life into empty downtowns.

title: Justice Dept. Is Investigating TV Networks Over Trump Pool Coverage
partialText: Major TV networks were notified on Friday that the department was examining whether they violated antitrust laws when they suspended pool coverage of President Trump.

title: What’s Dragging Down A.I. Efficiency? The ‘Verification Tax.’
partialText: As artificial intelligence automates office tasks, it is also creating a new type of human work.

title: Big Controversy Upends a Contest About Microscopic Videos
partialText: Nikon announced that it had disqualified the winner of its Small World in Motion competition over how A.I. was used in his submission.

title: Target Says It’s Not Working With ICE Amid Uproar Over Parking Lot Use
partialText: The retailer came under attack for being a staging area for immigration officers after Thursday’s shooting in New York City.

title: Trump Sends Obamacare ‘Refund’ Checks Ahead of Midterm Elections
partialText: The $500 checks are accompanied by a letter signed by the president that criticizes the Biden administration for overcharging Americans for health insurance.

title: Private Medicare Plans Are Raising Costs And Forcing Millions To Find New Insurance
partialText: As enrollment for Medicare Advantage begins this month, older Americans are confronting fewer options because insurers are discontinuing coverage in many areas.

title: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
partialText: The European Union said the deal could roughly halve shipments of hybrid vehicles from China in the next four years. But it also could lead to an even stronger Chinese auto industry.

title: Trump Announces White House Inquiry Into Fed Governor Lisa Cook
partialText: President Trump said the White House would investigate unsubstantiated claims that Lisa D. Cook committed mortgage fraud and hold a hearing next month.

title: How Correspondent Banking Can Enable Sanctions Evasion
partialText: The correspondent system for banking has enabled globalism — and has been exploited by companies trying to skirt U.S. sanctions.

title: Elon Musk, Delta Airlines and a Feud Over In-Flight Wi-Fi
partialText: Mr. Musk, whose company SpaceX owns Starlink, has attacked the top executive of Delta Air Lines for not selecting the internet provider.

title: The Fallout From OpenAI’s Revenue Surprise
partialText: News that the artificial intelligence giant’s sales weren’t growing as fast as investors had expected added to concerns about the A.I. boom.

title: The Winning Stock Funds This Time Weren’t Tech. They Were Energy.
partialText: Stock and bond fund returns for the quarter were bad nearly everywhere you looked, our columnist says. Energy stocks, lifted by the war with Iran, were an exception.

title: Wayne Lawson, Vanity Fair’s ‘Secret Weapon,’ Has Died
partialText: Working with Mr. Lawson, reporters said, was like taking a master class in writing: “He was a throwback to the old style of editing.”

title: What to Know About the Facebook Whistle-Blowing Case Depicted in ‘The Social Reckoning’
partialText: Aaron Sorkin’s sort-of sequel to the 2010 “Social Network” dramatizes a whistle-blowing case at Facebook. Here’s what to know.

title: Clara Wu Tsai, the Billionaire Who Wants Brooklyn to Win
partialText: Clara Wu Tsai, a co-owner of the Liberty and Nets, split from her husband of 30 years. Now she is turning her attention to leaving her mark on the borough.

title: Judge Extends Pause on Trump’s Ban Against CNN, MS NOW and Politico
partialText: The judge overseeing the case said that the pause would extend until next week, and promised to decide whether to further extend it by Tuesday.

title: Shifting Eating Habits Have PepsiCo Investors Seeking Operational Changes
partialText: Even though sales rose in the most recent quarter, the beverage and snack company is under increasing pressure to expand its business in North America, as consumers cut costs and calories.

title: Highest Mortgage Rates in 3 Years Chills the Housing Market
partialText: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.4 percent, putting more pressure on Americans struggling to afford to buy a home.

title: A.I. Fueled More Resilient Global Growth, W.T.O. Says
partialText: The World Trade Organization said that the drag on global trade from the war in the Middle East was more than offset by spending on goods related to artificial intelligence.

title: France Is Veering Toward a Potential Debt Crisis Amid Protests and Turmoil
partialText: French bond investors are demanding sharply higher interest rates, a cautionary development for other high-debt countries.

title: Oil Prices Jump on Outburst of Violence in the Middle East
partialText: Attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz have continued as a war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi militia intensified.

title: Amex Supersizes Newark Airport Centurion Lounge Before It Even Opens
partialText: To meet skyrocketing demand, lounge operators like American Express are racing to build bigger, and the Centurion in Newark’s Terminal A will be a giant.

title: The Little-Noticed Exception in Trump Accounts
partialText: Wealthy donors and companies can donate individual stocks to the new investment accounts for millions of children. That has raised legal questions.

title: Trump’s White House Ban on CNN, Politico and MS Now: What to Know
partialText: A judge temporarily blocked the president from barring journalists from White House grounds, but they are being excluded in other ways.

title: Can Your College Affect Your Income?
partialText: A new analysis of federal earnings data measures how much students who received federal financial aid earned four years after graduating. Our graphics reporter Arfa Momin studied the data to see when a graduate’s major and college mattered most to earnings.

title: How the Trump Administration Is Eroding Airline Passengers’ Rights
partialText: Under Sean Duffy, the Transportation Department has worked to roll back consumer protections. Passenger advocates say the changes favor airlines.

title: A Top Fed Official Casts Further Doubt on a Rate Rise This Month
partialText: The Federal Reserve is poised to raise interest rates further as it seeks to tame inflation, but that is unlikely to happen until the end of the year.
